title: fig04 reworked (2026-08-03 lock retracted): spectrogram-block/trace-block layout + band-power-vs-context-x-family GLMM
notes: Unsealed the 2026-08-03 fig04 lock (seal_checkpoint_20260803_fig04_locked.json) per explicit user direction to rework the figure.
Layout reworked: build_v1_pfc_condition_figure() now draws two stacked 4x2 blocks (all spectrograms, then all traces) instead of interleaved per-area-row columns.

extract_condition_tfr_maps.py's CONDS extended from R-family-only (RXRR/RRXR/RRRR) to add AXAB/AAAB (A-family) and BXBA/BBBA (B-family) p2-matched pairs -- no new NWB pass, all 12 GLO_CONDITIONS .npy arrays already existed in D:/workspace/data/tfr_arrays. Full re-extraction ran ~97 min (707 files), producing outputs/condition_tfr_maps_p1d1p2d2p3/maps.npz with 2471 keys across 10 areas x 7 conditions.

New GLMM: per area x band (20 cells, 4 areas x 5 bands), M0: db~C(context)+C(family) vs M1: M0+C(context):C(family), groups=animal random intercept, ML fit for valid LR comparison. Tests the hypothesis that LFP band power tracks network state/prior over context (omission vs stimulus) and whether that depends on stimulus identity (A/B/R family).

Result: 15/20 area x band cells show a significant family-pooled context effect (Holm-corrected) -- power higher for a real stimulus than omission, consistent across V1 (all 5 bands), most of V3a/d and TEO, and theta/alpha/beta in PFC. 0/20 context x family interaction tests survive correction -- no evidence the relationship depends on stimulus identity in this corpus.

Caught and fixed a real sign-labeling bug during review: patsy's default reference level for context is 'omission' (alphabetically first), so the fitted coefficient is literally stimulus-minus-omission, not omission-minus-stimulus as first labeled. Added an assert on the exact patsy term name so a future data change that altered reference-level choice would fail loudly rather than silently mislabel the sign.

Caught and fixed three layout bugs during review, each found only by rendering and visually inspecting, not by reasoning about the numbers: (1) header text (suptitle/legend) positioned at figure-fraction y>1.0 was silently clipped by plain savefig (no bbox_inches='tight'); (2) a rect-based tight_layout guess left a large dead gap above the panel grid; (3) a min()-clamp on the suptitle's y-position was set below the axes' actual measured top, pushing the title into the plot. Final fix places header elements from axes[0,0].get_position().y1 (measured, not guessed) with a fixed clearance for the per-panel title.

fig04.png is now a PIL vertical stack of the two component PNGs (grid + GLMM), not a re-render of the assembled SVG -- the finalized PNG is still owed via headless Chrome once panel content is approved, same as figs 1-3's convention.

Session also: fixed a real 6.7GB duplicate-cache bug in jnwb/session.py (CWD-relative cache path silently created a second full NWB table cache when a script was run from a different working directory) and anchored it to the repo root; deleted the accidental duplicate. D: drive audit found no other duplicate/stale data -- the 96%-full state is legitimate (2.7TB raw NWB + 1.7TB derived TFR arrays), not junk accumulation.
issues: fig04 is NOT locked/sealed -- the 2026-08-03 seal was explicitly retracted by this rework and no new seal has been written. Needs user review of panel content (layout, GLMM framing) before any lock/finalized-PNG step.
fig04.png (working preview) is a PIL stack, not a true render of fig04.svg -- do not treat it as equivalent to the finalized-PNG convention until the headless-Chrome step is done.

GLMM's animal random-intercept variance is weakly identified with only 3 animals in this corpus -- reported as-is with convergence_notes captured, not suppressed, but this is a real power limitation worth stating in any manuscript text drawing on these results.
fig05/06/07 still not locked (unchanged from the 2026-08-04 drift checklist earlier this session) -- this fig04 work does not touch that backlog.
plan: Next: get user sign-off on fig04's reworked panel content (layout + GLMM framing/results), then produce fig04_finalized.svg/.png via headless Chrome and write a new seal checkpoint, following the fig01-04 (original) lock pattern.
Consider whether the GLMM's context-pooled result (15/20 cells) and null interaction result (0/20) belong in a manuscript supplement or the main fig04 caption once locked.
